typography.$description: Real-usage audit (2026-07-23) found a genuine gap this scale doesn't cover: 13px recurs heavily across 3 of the 5 apps (career-web, client-web, recruitment-portal — 116+ combined instances) sitting right between paragraph-xsmall (12px) and paragraph-small (14px). RESOLUTION (2026-07-25): not formalized as its own token — 13px is almost certainly Figma/rem-rounding drift (0.8125rem is an unusually precise, non-round rem value for a deliberate design choice) rather than an intentional size. Recommended fix at the code level: snap any text-[13px] usage to paragraph-small (14px), the single most dominant body size in every app, rather than inventing a permanent token to match an accident. Two related weight consolidations applied in this pass: heading-h5/h6 moved from an unconfirmed Semibold(600) guess to Medium(500), since Medium is the single most-evidenced weight in this entire file (5/5 confirmed wherever it appears) versus Semibold's weaker 3/5 confirmation rate — the safer default until real data says otherwise. display-small (44px) is deprecated in favor of heading-h1 (40px) — see its entry below. Typography is also now emitted as composite Tailwind component classes (e.g. .text-heading-h2 bundling size+line-height+weight+tracking in one class) rather than relying on separately-applied text-size + font-weight utilities that can drift apart — see the tokens repo's build.mjs.

sans.$description: The font actually rendered in all 5 apps today, applied via a global CSS override rather than Tailwind config. This token is what fixes that — register it as the Tailwind 'sans' default.

mono.$description: New token — no app currently defines a mono stack. Proposed for code/data display.

display-large.$description: Weight changed 2026-07-25 from Bold(700) to Extrabold(800), following directly from heading-h2's conflict resolution: Bold(700) was never confirmed by an actual Figma variable anywhere in this file, and the one real Figma instance that rendered as Bold (the Title component, at heading-h2's size) turned out to be the drifted value, not the canonical one — the ratified foundation-page weight was Extrabold. Matching display-large to its now-resolved neighbors (heading-h1/h2, both 800) removes Bold as a separate, never-confirmed tier. Still a proposed default for this specific size, not itself confirmed. Real-usage audit (2026-07-23): rare but real — dead in 3 of 5 apps, used in the other 2 at low volume (4-8 instances each).

display-small.$description: ⚠️ DEPRECATED (2026-07-25) in favor of heading-h1 (40px). Real-usage audit (2026-07-23): this was the weakest size in the entire type scale — dead in 3 of 5 apps, and only 1 real usage each in the other 2 (a single arbitrary instance apiece). Sitting 4px from heading-h1 (solidly used in 4 of 5 apps) with no evidence anyone needs the distinction, this token is kept only so nothing that already references it breaks — new work should use heading-h1 directly. Remove entirely once nothing points to it.

heading-h1.$description: Weight proposed by extrapolation from the confirmed H2 weight, not itself confirmed. Real-usage audit (2026-07-23): solidly used in 4 of 5 apps (only career-web has zero real usage) — a real, load-bearing size, unlike its close neighbor display-small (44px).

heading-h2.$description: RESOLVED (2026-07-25), by explicit design decision: the Typography foundation page's own named Figma variable says 'Heading/H2/Extrabold/Desktop' (800, used here), but the Title component's live design context showed the same 36/44 size rendered as Inter Bold — weight 700, not 800. The foundation page is ratified as canonical; the Title component's Bold rendering is the thing that drifted and should be corrected in Figma/components to match this token, not the other way around.

heading-h3.$description: Confirmed via live Figma design context on the Stat component ('Heading/H3/Semibold/Desktop', weight 600) — corrected from an earlier proposed guess of 700.

heading-h5.$description: Weight changed 2026-07-25 from an unconfirmed Semibold(600) guess to Medium(500) — Medium is confirmed 5/5 times everywhere it appears in this file (the strongest weight-evidence of any tier), versus Semibold's weaker 3/5 confirmation rate. Still a default, not a confirmed value for this specific size, but the safer one.

heading-h6.$description: Weight changed 2026-07-25 from an unconfirmed Semibold(600) guess to Medium(500), same reasoning as heading-h5 — Medium is the most reliably-confirmed weight in this file.

paragraph-large-medium.$description: Confirmed twice — a named Figma variable ('Paragraph/Large/Medium'), and again via live design context on the Modal component's heading text.

paragraph-large-semibold.$description: New — confirmed via live Figma design context on the Accordion component's title text (Inter Semibold 18/28). Same size as paragraph-large-regular/medium, a third weight in the same size family.

paragraph-medium-medium.$description: Confirmed via live Figma design context on the Button component (Size=Large label uses Inter Medium 16/24) — same size as paragraph-medium, Medium weight instead of Regular, same pairing pattern as paragraph-large-regular/medium.

paragraph-small.$description: Confirmed twice via live Figma design context: Input Field (Box and Line variants, value/placeholder/helper text) and Modal (description text).

paragraph-small-medium.$description: Confirmed twice via live Figma design context: Button (Size=Medium label) and Input Field (label text) both use Inter Medium 14/20.

paragraph-xsmall.$description: Confirmed via live Figma design context on the Tooltip component's description text ('Paragraph/XSmall/Regular'). Corrected lineHeight from an earlier proposed guess of 20px to the real 16px.

label-xsmall.$description: Confirmed repeatedly via live Figma design context: Button (Size=Small label), Avatar Group overflow badge, Tab badge, and Table Content Cell's avatar-group overflow badge all use this exact 12/15 Medium style. Distinct from paragraph-xsmall: same fontSize but a tighter 15px line-height and Medium weight. CORRECTED 2026-07-25: 'Side Nav Item badge' was removed from this list — a real-code audit of all 5 apps found no badge/count-indicator element anywhere in any real Side Navigation implementation; this was a Figma-only claim that didn't survive contact with real code.

overline.$description: Confirmed via live Figma design context on the Table Header component ('Paragraph/Overline/Small', uppercase in usage) — corrected fontSize/lineHeight/letterSpacing/weight from an earlier proposed guess.
